# Jubilees Chapter 46 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Joseph and his brothers' deaths; Israel multiplies in Egypt

---

**46:1** And after Jacob's death the children of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became great and mighty, and the land was full of them.

**46:2** And Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, died. And all the Egyptians were grieved for him many days. And a new king of Egypt arose, who did not know Joseph.

**46:3** And Joseph's brothers said to him: "Now that our father is dead, perhaps Joseph will hate us and will repay us all the evil which we did unto him." And they sent a message to Joseph, saying: "Thy father commanded before he died, saying: 'Forgive thy brothers and pardon all their transgressions.'"

**46:4** And Joseph was grieved, and wept when his brothers came to him, and fell down before him. And Joseph said to them: "Fear not, for am I in the place of God? As for you, you thought evil against me; but God meant it for good, to bring to pass as it is this day — to save many lives. Therefore, fear not. I will nourish you and your little ones."

**46:5** And Joseph lived after his father's death fifty-five years. And all the days of Joseph's life were one hundred and ten years. And Joseph died.

**46:6** And before he died he commanded his sons, saying: "When I die, carry me up with my bones from this land to the land of Canaan." And he made them swear.

**46:7** And all the brothers of Joseph died — Reuben and Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Zebulun and Dan and Gad and Asher and Naphtali. All the sons of Jacob died in the land of Egypt in the fiftieth year of the fiftieth jubilee.

**46:8** And the children of Israel were fruitful and increased greatly and multiplied and became very strong, and the land was filled with them.

**46:9** And Pharaoh saw that the land was full of them, and he was afraid. And he acted with craftiness and said to his servants: "Let us deal wisely with Israel, lest they multiply and it come to pass that if there be a war, they also will be added to our enemies and fight against us and go out of the land."

**46:10** And they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with heavy labor. And they built store-cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses. And the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad.

---

*EMET notes: Chapter 46 covers Genesis 50:15-26 and Exodus 1:1-14. The reconciliation scene (vv.3-4) repeats Joseph's "you meant evil, God meant good" speech. The death of all twelve sons (v.7) is dated in Jubilees to the fiftieth year of the fiftieth jubilee. The beginning of the oppression (vv.9-10) follows Exodus 1.*
